quiz.question_en: Why does `listTodos` use `mu.RLock()` while `createTodo` and `deleteTodo` use `mu.Lock()`?
options_id: Karena membaca data bisa berbagi lock, sedangkan mutasi map harus eksklusif
Karena `RLock` selalu lebih cepat untuk semua operasi
Karena `Lock` hanya boleh dipakai pada POST
options_en: Because reads can share a lock, while mutating the map must be exclusive
Because `RLock` is always faster for every operation
Because `Lock` may only be used for POST
Because the JSON encoder requires `RLock`

quiz.question_id: Mengapa validasi `input.Title == ""` sebaiknya dilakukan sebelum memasuki critical section yang memodifikasi store?
quiz.question_en: Why is validating `input.Title == ""` best done before entering the critical section that mutates the store?
options_id: Agar request invalid ditolak lebih awal tanpa memegang lock lebih lama dari perlu
Karena string kosong bisa membuat mutex panic
Karena `json.Decoder` hanya bekerja di luar lock
options_en: So invalid requests are rejected early without holding the lock longer than necessary
Because an empty string can make the mutex panic
So `nextID` is automatically reset
Because `json.Decoder` only works outside a lock

quiz.question_id: Route registration mana yang sesuai dengan handler delete pada sample?
quiz.question_en: Which route registration matches the delete handler in the sample?
options_en: `mux.HandleFunc("DELETE /todos/{id}", deleteTodo)`
`mux.HandleFunc("/todos/delete/{id}", deleteTodo)`
`mux.HandleFunc("POST /todos/{id}/delete", deleteTodo)`
`mux.HandleFunc("DELETE /todos?id={id}", deleteTodo)`

options_id: Karena path parameter dibaca sebagai string, sedangkan map `todos` menggunakan key `int`
Karena `Atoi` sekaligus mengecek apakah todo ada
Karena route DELETE selalu mengirim angka biner
options_en: Because the path parameter is read as a string, while the `todos` map uses `int` keys
Because `PathValue` returns JSON
Because `Atoi` also checks whether the todo exists
Because DELETE routes always send a binary number

quiz.question_id: Kombinasi status code mana yang benar untuk `deleteTodo` bila `id` invalid versus todo tidak ditemukan?
quiz.question_en: Which status code combination is correct in `deleteTodo` for an invalid `id` versus a missing todo?
options_en: 400 then 404
404 then 400
401 then 404
400 then 204

quiz.question_id: Mengapa `nextID++` sebaiknya dilakukan saat lock masih dipegang?
quiz.question_en: Why should `nextID++` happen while the lock is still held?
options_id: Agar pembuatan ID dan penyimpanan todo menjadi satu operasi sinkron yang aman dari race
Karena `nextID` tidak bisa diubah di luar function
options_en: So ID assignment and todo storage stay as one synchronized operation safe from races
Because `nextID` cannot be changed outside the function
So the status code automatically becomes 201
Because `json.NewEncoder` requires the newest ID

quiz.question_id: Mengapa response sukses untuk DELETE menggunakan `http.StatusNoContent`?
quiz.question_en: Why does the successful DELETE response use `http.StatusNoContent`?
options_id: Karena operasi berhasil dan handler tidak mengirim body response
Karena DELETE tidak boleh berhasil dengan kode lain
Karena client harus redirect setelah delete
options_en: Because the operation succeeded and the handler does not send a response body
Because DELETE may not succeed with any other code
Because the resource has not actually been deleted yet
Because the client must redirect after delete

quiz.question_id: Registrasi method-specific routing mana yang sesuai untuk pembuatan todo?
quiz.question_en: Which method-specific route registration matches todo creation?
options_en: `mux.HandleFunc("POST /todos", createTodo)`
`mux.HandleFunc("/todos", createTodo)` alone without a method
`mux.Handle("POST", createTodo)`
`mux.Post("/todos", createTodo)`

quiz.question_id: Jika `deleteTodo` memakai `RLock` lalu tetap memanggil `delete(todos, id)`, masalah konsep utamanya apa?
quiz.question_en: If `deleteTodo` used `RLock` and still called `delete(todos, id)`, what would be the main conceptual problem?
options_id: Itu hanya memperlambat sedikit, tapi tetap benar
Ia mencoba memodifikasi shared map di bawah read lock, yang tidak aman
Status code akan otomatis berubah ke 500
options_en: It would only be slightly slower but still correct
It would be mutating a shared map under a read lock, which is unsafe
The status code would automatically change to 500
`r.PathValue` does not work with `RLock`

quiz.question_id: Apa alasan utama `sync.RWMutex` diperlukan pada store in-memory di server HTTP ini?
quiz.question_en: What is the main reason `sync.RWMutex` is needed for this in-memory store in an HTTP server?
options_id: Karena setiap request HTTP dapat berjalan bersamaan dan map Go tidak aman untuk concurrent mutation/read tanpa sinkronisasi
Karena JSON encoder selalu menuntut mutex
options_en: Because HTTP requests can run concurrently and Go maps are not safe for concurrent mutation/read without synchronization
Because the JSON encoder always demands a mutex
Because the `{id}` route path must be locked
Because `http.ListenAndServe` only works with a mutex
